title: Resilience after multiplying by parity
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a set of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with $|S|=k+1$, and let $g:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$. Suppose $g$ depends only on coordinates outside $S$. Then the function obtained by multiplying $g$ pointwise by the parity of the coordinates in $S$ is $k$-resilient: it is balanced and all its nonconstant Fourier coefficients indexed by sets of size at most $k$ vanish.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a finite set of coordinates among $n$ coordinates
$g$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
